Lesson 1 · Render vs commit

Render can be thrown away. Commit can't.

Render phaseCommit phase
What happensReact calls your components and diffs the resultReact updates the DOM, refs and layout effects
RulesPure. No fetching, no DOM writesSide effects belong here
Pause or discard?Yes, for non-urgent workNo. Runs in one go
StrictMode (dev)Called twiceEffects run setup, cleanup, setup
Render can run many times or be thrown away. Keep it pure.
MODULE 05 · VIDEO 1
04 / 42
Lesson 1 · Fiber and lanes, plainly

Pausable work, ranked by urgency

Typing “rea” starts a transition: React renders the list one fiber at a time.Between slices it yields, so the browser can paint and take input.A key lands. Urgent lane first, and the half-built list for “rea” is thrown away.The input commits “reac” straight away: the user sees their keystroke.The transition restarts with “reac”……slice by slice, yielding in between……and no newer key arrives, so this time it finishes.Commit: the whole list lands in one go. Nobody saw a half-built list.

Fiber · one unit of work

One object per component. React can stop after any fiber and resume later.

Lane · a priority

A priority per update. Typing is urgent; startTransition work can wait and restart.

React builds the next tree off-screen, so throwing it away is safe.

Lesson 1 · useTransition

Keep typing urgent. Let the list wait.

function SearchBox({ onSearch }: { onSearch: (q: string) => void }) {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();

  function onChange(e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
    setText(e.target.value);                         // urgent: the input
    startTransition(() => onSearch(e.target.value)); // can wait: the list
  }

  return <><input value={text} onChange={onChange} />{isPending && <Spinner />}</>;
}
// FeedPage: const [query, setQuery] = useState('');  →  <SearchBox onSearch={setQuery} />
try it · type fast isPending keystroke → paint– renders dropped0
5,000 match
text stays urgent. The list renders in slices and restarts on every new key.

Lesson 2 · Anatomy of a re-render

Four reasons a component runs again

1 · Its state changed

setSaved(true) with a new value. Same value? React bails out.

2 · Its parent rendered

Its children run again by default, props changed or not.

3 · A context it reads changed

Readers render when the provider's value changes.

4 · A hook it calls changed

A custom hook's state is the component's state.

“Its props changed” isn't on the list. New props only arrive because the parent rendered. memo opts out of reason 2.

      Lesson 3 · Stale closures in effects

      An effect that runs once remembers the first render

      Stale: saves an empty draft forever

      useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(
    () => saveDraft(letter), 10_000);
  return () => clearInterval(id);
}, []); // letter frozen at ''

      Fresh: read the latest from a ref

      const latest = useRef(letter);
useEffect(() => { latest.current = letter; });

useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(
    () => saveDraft(latest.current), 10_000);
  return () => clearInterval(id);
}, []); // one timer, newest value
      try it · auto-save every 3 s
      stale effect saved: ref effect saved:
      Fix it with a dependency (the timer restarts) or a ref (one timer, latest value). Never silence the lint rule.

      Lesson 3 · The effect you might not need

      Derive it. Don't synchronise it.

      Synchronised: two renders, one stale

      const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
const [visible, setVisible] =
  useState<Listing[]>([]);

useEffect(() => {
  setVisible(
    listings.filter(l => matches(l, query)));
}, [listings, query]);

      Derived: computed during render

      const [query, setQuery] = useState('');

const visible = listings.filter(
  l => matches(l, query));

// one render, always in step

      Lesson 4 · Controlled vs uncontrolled

      Who owns the value? Support both.

      Controlled · the parent owns it

      <SearchBox value={q} onChange={setQ} />
      parent sees""parent renders0

      Uncontrolled · the component owns it

      <SearchBox defaultValue="react" />
      parent sees—parent renders0
      function useControllableState<T>(value: T | undefined, defaultValue: T, onChange?: (v: T) => void) {
  const [inner, setInner] = useState(defaultValue);
  const isControlled = value !== undefined;
  const current = isControlled ? value : inner;
  function set(next: T) {
    if (!isControlled) setInner(next);   // uncontrolled: keep it ourselves
    onChange?.(next);                     // either way: tell the parent
  }
  return [current, set] as const;
}

        Lesson 5 · Build · Race conditions

        Whichever response lands last wins

        Debounce cuts how many requests start, not the order they land in.

        on screen: —“react” results ✓“re” results ✗ stale
        Debounce is a cost fix. Cancelling the stale request is the correctness fix.

        Lesson 5 · Build · Debounce and abort

        One effect: wait, fetch, cancel

        useEffect(() => {
  if (query.trim().length < 2) { setJobs([]); return; }
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {                          // debounce: wait for a pause
    fetch('/api/jobs?q=' + encodeURIComponent(query), { signal: ctrl.signal })
      .then(res => res.json())
      .then(setJobs)
      .catch(err => { if (!ctrl.signal.aborted) setError(err); });
  }, 250);
  return () => { clearTimeout(timer); ctrl.abort(); };   // the next keystroke cancels both
}, [query]);
        The query changed: a fresh AbortController for this run.Wait 250 ms for the typing to pause.Then fetch, wired to the controller's signal.Next keystroke: the cleanup clears the timer and aborts the fetch. A stale answer never reaches setJobs.
        The cleanup is the fix: each keystroke clears the timer and aborts the request in flight.

        Lesson 6 · Build · The modal

        Trap focus, then give it back

        function openModal() {
  returnTo.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;   // remember the trigger
  setOpen(true);                                               // an effect focuses the first field
}
function onKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent) {
  if (e.key === 'Escape') return closeModal();
  if (e.key !== 'Tab') return;
  const items = Array.from(panel.current!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE));
  const first = items[0], last = items[items.length - 1];
  if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) { e.preventDefault(); last.focus(); }
  if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) { e.preventDefault(); first.focus(); }
}
function closeModal() { setOpen(false); returnTo.current?.focus(); }

        Lesson 6 · Build · Toasts and live regions

        Announce it without moving focus

        // Mounted once, empty, at the app root: a live region must exist before its text changes
<div role="status" className="sr-only">{announcement}</div>

function toast(message: string) {
  setToasts(list => [...list, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), message }]);   // the visible stack
  setAnnouncement('');                                                   // clear first, so the same
  setTimeout(() => setAnnouncement(message), 50);                        // text twice is still read
}

        Lesson 7 · Forms without a library

        Keep the rules, own the messages

        <form noValidate onSubmit={onSubmit}>                  {/* keep the checks, drop the browser bubbles */}
  <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required
    aria-invalid={Boolean(errors.email)} aria-describedby="email-error" />
  <p id="email-error">{errors.email}</p>
</form>

function messageFor(input: HTMLInputElement) {
  const v = input.validity;                              // the browser already ran the rules
  if (v.valueMissing) return 'This field is required';
  if (v.typeMismatch) return 'Check the format, like name@company.com';
  if (v.tooShort)     return 'Use at least ' + input.minLength + ' characters';
  return '';
}

        Lesson 7 · Validation timing

        Submit checks all; blur checks one

        function onSubmit(e: React.SubmitEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
  e.preventDefault();
  const form = e.currentTarget;
  const next = validate(form);                        // messageFor() on every field → { name: message }
  setErrors(next);
  const first = Object.keys(next)[0];
  if (first) return (form.elements.namedItem(first) as HTMLElement).focus();
  apply(new FormData(form));                           // valid: send it
}
        WhenWhat you do
        SubmitCheck all, show all, focus the first error
        BlurCheck that field, if it changed
        TypingClear a fixed error. Never add one mid-word

        Lesson 8 · Writing the boundary

        Still a class, and it can't catch everything

        class ErrorBoundary extends Component<Props, { failed: boolean }> {
  state = { failed: false };
  static getDerivedStateFromError() {
    return { failed: true }; // show fallback
  }
  componentDidCatch(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo) {
    logError(error, info.componentStack);
  }
  render() {
    return this.state.failed
      ? this.props.fallback
      : this.props.children;
  }
}
        Thrown while…Caught?
        Rendering below ityes
        An effect below ityes
        An event handlerno: try/catch + error state
        A timer or .thenno
        The boundary itselfno: the next one up
        Still no hook in React 19. Write the class once, reuse it with a different fallback.
